PILLOWCASE — LABORATORY

On 14 January 2030 at 06.20, on the fourth floor of a capsule hotel in Shinjuku, a man was found dead in upper capsule 4B-12. The cleaner opened it after hearing an alarm ringing for twenty minutes from the capsule with its curtain down.

According to the hotel register, the guest in 4B-12 is “Kimura Shin”. But the driving licence in the body’s wallet belongs to Tanabe Kōji (41): a sales representative from Osaka. Tanabe’s hotel registration is for **4B-11**.

Patrol note: “Smell of alcohol. Heart attack or choking in his sleep. The capsules got mixed up; the hotel’s mistake.”

A register tells you not who slept where, but who was supposed to sleep where. First ask who died, then who was meant to die.
Shinjuku, Tokyo — January 2030

Kisaragi Shōji accountant Mori Kenta copied the company’s ledgers and hid in a capsule hotel under the name ‘Kimura Shin’. In the night he swapped wristbands and places with Tanabe Kōji, who could not sleep because of the snoring next door. The company’s security consultant Ōta Ren bought the capsule number and the floor card from the receptionist, entered 4B-12 at 01.31 and smothered the man inside with a pillow. The dead man was Tanabe, not Mori.
